notes: The chats the bot delivers into, one per notify level. A producer asks for a level by name - 'warning', 'logging' - and the message goes wherever that name points here, which is why muting a stream means clearing this file rather than editing code.

One chat covers both levels in this quickstart, because the point is to see a message arrive rather than to design a routing scheme. In a real estate they are separate chats: 'logging' is the record and is high-volume by design, 'warning' is the one somebody reads.

'group_id' is negative for a group and positive for a direct message. REPLACE the placeholder with your own - the id below belongs to nobody and delivery will fail with 'chat not found', which is the correct failure for a chat that does not exist.
The fastest way to learn your own id: message your bot, then run 'python -m db_ops.telegram.cli --config config.json get-updates' and read chat.id out of the reply.

'allow_command' is the highest command clearance this chat may exercise. 0 means the bot delivers here and accepts no commands from here, which is what a quickstart wants - this file can otherwise let a stranger's chat drive the toolkit.
